claims.text: The target initial material is a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy in an as-cast or homogenized condition without deliberate carbon additions.
Low-level carbon addition followed by controlled aging will promote carbide precipitation.
The resulting carbide precipitates will be nanoscale and coherent with the matrix.
The carbide precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the matrix.
The carbide precipitates will hinder dislocation movement through precipitation strengthening.
Precipitation strengthening will reduce high-temperature softening.
Carbon addition and aging will enhance elevated-temperature yield strength.
The treated alloy will show a moderate to significant yield-strength improvement relative to an identical untreated alloy.
An alloy without carbon addition and controlled aging typically exhibits more pronounced high-temperature softening.
The strengthening effect should be observable at service temperatures around 850 K and above.
The proposed effect should persist across temperatures above approximately 850 K up to temperatures below the alloy's melting point.
The magnitude of yield-strength improvement will depend on alloy composition, carbon level, and aging parameters.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as receiving neither carbon nor controlled aging, whereas the experimental control is described as processed identically to the carbon-added set except for carbon addition, which implies that it may receive the aging treatment. These are not the same baseline.
